Avenger Air Defense Missiles Deployed Near Trump’s Mar-a-Lago Resort — The US Secret Service has deployed two Avenger surface-to-air missile systems on a floating barge near US President Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago estate in Florida following warnings of an elevated, dynamic threat environment. The Humvee-mounted Stinger missile systems provide specialized low-altitude defense against drones, cruise missiles, and low-flying aircraft.

Trump Tinkers — Despite calling himself a great dealmaker, the US president, in his attempt to negotiate a peace deal between Russia and Ukraine, has always made concessions to Moscow with nothing in return. If this is great dealmaking, then it begs the question: Who is Trump working for?

Drones and Neptune Missiles Strike Kamensky Rocket Fuel Plant — Ukrainian Defense Forces conducted a complex overnight strike using attack drones and Navy Neptune missile systems against the Kamensky chemical plant in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, Rostov region, the General Staff announced on Saturday, Oct. 31. The precision attack ignited a finished goods warehouse and damaged four production workshops at the facility, which synthesizes solid rocket propellant for Uragan, Smerch, and Tornado-S artillery

Russian Energy Strikes Cut Power to 280,000 Across Ukraine — Coordinated Russian missile and drone strikes on Oct. 30 damaged combined heat and power plants, four electrical substations, gas distribution hubs, and rail infrastructure across Kyiv, Dnipro, Shostka, and Kharkiv, leaving roughly 280,000 families without electricity, President Volodymyr Zelensky announced. The attacks knocked out power to 200,000 households in Dnipropetrovsk region and over 80,000 in Kyiv region as repair crews mobil

Russian War Casualties Up to 2.1 Million – The Economist — A study published by The Economist estimates Russian military casualties at between 1.4 million and 2.1 million killed and wounded, with fatalities ranging from 374,000 to 770,000. In comparison, tracking site UALosses records 116,000 Ukrainian soldiers killed and 106,000 missing. The study notes that Ukrainian forces recaptured 73 square kilometers of territory over the last three months, erasing half of Russia’s 2026 land gains, while

Lavrov Protests Poland’s G20 Role as US Backs Full Membership — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov criticized the US on Friday, Oct. 30, for inviting Poland to participate as a full member in G20 ministerial meetings in Atlanta, claiming the unilateral invitation violated consensus rules. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio defended Warsaw, arguing Poland’s $1 trillion economy and regional leadership justify permanent membership alongside France and Germany.

4 Planes With Oleshky Evacuees Land in Belarus En Route to Kyiv — Four aircraft carrying Ukrainian civilians evacuated from the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky landed in Gomel, Belarus, on Saturday, Oct. 31, ahead of their final bus transfer across the border into Ukraine, parliamentary leader David Arakhamia announced. The multi-stage evacuation was coordinated by Ukrainian human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets and Russian counterpart Yana Lantratova under an 87-hour localized ceasefire me

Newly Approved $2.1B Patriot Missile Sale Faces Post-2030 Delivery — The US approved a $2.1 billion Foreign Military Sale of 500 Patriot PAC-3 MSE interceptors to Ukraine, but deliveries are projected not to begin until after 2030. The post-2030 timeline does not alleviate Ukraine’s immediate interceptor deficit ahead of winter, while Pentagon reviews on domestic coproduction licenses remain unresolved.

Merz Announces Berlin ‘Coalition of the Willing’ Summit — German Chancellor Friedrich Merz announced on Saturday, Oct. 31, that Germany will host a meeting of the “Coalition of the Willing” in Berlin in mid-November to coordinate international military and financial assistance for Ukraine.

Drones Hit Bashneft-Novoil Refinery in Ufa — Long-range Ukrainian strike drones targeted the northern industrial hub of Ufa in Russia’s Republic of Bashkortostan overnight into Saturday, Oct. 31, igniting a major fire at the “Bashneft-Novoil” oil refinery and reportedly engaging the neighboring Bashneft-UNPZ plant. Flames engulfed the L-35 catalytic reforming unit, which produces high-octane gasoline reformate and hydrogen for desulfurization.

Poland in Constitutional Standoff as Court Heads Suspended — Poland entered an acute constitutional crisis on Friday, Oct. 30, after Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska issued orders suspending Constitutional Tribunal President Bogdan Święczkowski and his deputy Bartłomiej Sochański for one month, assuming acting leadership under Article 130 of the courts statute. President Karol Nawrocki reversed his state flight to Senegal to return to Warsaw as police entered the court building amid violent protests

Trump Criticizes Russia Sanctions Calls, Citing Hubbard Release — US President Donald Trump criticized demands for new sanctions against Russia on Friday, Oct. 30, arguing that economic penalties would have prevented the release of 74-year-old American citizen Stephen Hubbard from a Russian prison. Hubbard, a Michigan native detained in Ukraine in April 2022 and convicted on mercenary charges, was released on Oct. 21 during talks in St. Petersburg between Russian President Vladimir Putin and US

US Eyes December Decision on Permanent Military Base in Poland — The US is expected to decide in December whether to establish its first permanent military base in Poland, Polish Deputy Defense Minister Stanisław Wziątek announced on Friday, Oct. 30. A Pentagon posture review is nearing completion, though an announcement could extend into early next year. General Dariusz Łukowski, former head of Poland’s National Security Bureau, estimated the project would cost 3 billion zloty (€700 million) pl

Canada Pledges €500M Toward EU’s €90B Ukraine Loan — Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announced on Friday, Oct. 30 that Canada will contribute €500 million as an initial commitment toward the EU’s €90 billion loan facility for Ukraine. Speaking alongside Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa at the 21st EU-Canada summit in Montreal, Carney commended the mechanism for leveraging immobilized Russian assets.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, October 30, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on October 30, 2026.

Poland Calls for Urgent Black Sea Ceasefire, Demands Fair Peace for Ukraine — Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski called for an urgent Black Sea ceasefire to protect grain shipments from Ukraine and Russia, while insisting that Moscow should not regain access to European energy markets without a fair end to its invasion. He also rejected any peace process that excludes Kyiv or Europe.

Cracks in ‘One Nation, Two States’ – Why Aliyev Is Distancing Himself From Turkey and Embracing Russia — Erdoğan’s closing prayer at the Turkic summit took on new significance as Aliyev stayed away amid growing tensions. Beyond the headscarf controversy, the rift reflects disputes over Turkey’s role in Azerbaijan’s Karabakh victory, Baku’s ties with Israel and Aliyev’s renewed engagement with Moscow.

Russian Strike Leaves Large Parts of Kyiv Without Water as Crews Race to Restore Services — Russian drone strikes on Kyiv’s critical infrastructure disrupted water supplies across much of the capital Friday night. Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported three direct hits on one facility, leaving several districts without water and others with reduced pressure as emergency crews worked to restore services.

Pentagon Says Ukraine’s Patriot Missile Production Request Requires ‘Further Review’ — The Pentagon has referred Ukraine’s request to manufacture Patriot interceptors for further review, leaving Kyiv without a production license or timeline. The unresolved issue comes as Ukraine faces interceptor shortages and warnings that newly approved US missile deliveries could take years.

Russia Strikes Kharkiv With Jet-Powered Shahed Drone, Injuring 3, Damaging 10 Homes — A Russian jet-powered Shahed drone struck Kharkiv’s Osnovianskyi district, injuring three civilians and damaging 10 residential buildings. The attack followed another strike on a shopping center, as Moscow continues its intensive drone campaign against the northeastern city.

EU, Canada Vow More Pressure on Russia as Ottawa Moves to Join €90 Billion Ukraine Defense Loan — At the Montreal summit, EU and Canadian leaders pledged continued military and financial support for Ukraine, stronger pressure on Russia and accountability for wartime crimes. Ottawa also announced plans to participate in the EU’s €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan, opening a potential new route for Ukrainian weapons procurement.

US Approves 500 Patriot Missiles for Ukraine, but Zelensky Warns Deliveries May Not Begin for Years — President Volodymyr Zelensky welcomed Washington’s approval of a $2.1 billion Patriot missile sale but warned that deliveries might not begin for several years. He urged the US and its allies to release existing interceptors immediately and replenish their arsenals with newly manufactured missiles.

Ukraine Allocates $7.8M to Repair Shelters in Maternity Hospitals — Ukraine’s government, led by Prime Minister Serhii Koretskyi, announced on Friday, Oct. 30 that it is allocating Hr. 354.6 million ($7.8 million) in total to repair shelters in 84 maternity facilities and strengthen hospital protection. The funds will be reallocated within the Health Ministry’s budget, though officials did not specify which hospitals or cities the funds are intended for.

Amber Infrastructure Plans 10-15 Year Exits as 2 Ukraine Funds Hunt ‘Ready-to-Build’ Projects — Amber Infrastructure runs two Ukraine funds worth a combined €467 million ($523 million) raised from international financial institutions and European public money. Managing Director and Ukraine Lead Dominykas Tuckus explained to Kyiv Post that the funds co-invest in the same assets, target wind, distributed energy and logistics, and are built for exits over 10 to 15 years.

US Midterm Early Voting Hits Record 48 Million — A record 47.9 million Americans have voted early in the US midterm elections, surpassing the 2022 record of 45.9 million, according to the University of Florida’s Election Lab. Registered Democrats have outpaced Republicans in early ballots, though experts warn the figures do not predict the outcome.

Canada and EU Launch New Alliance Covering Ukraine, Critical Minerals and AI — Canada and the EU launched a new alliance at a summit in Montreal amid strained ties with Washington, agreeing to deepen cooperation on critical minerals, artificial intelligence and digital trade. Canada will also join the EU’s €90 billion support loan for Ukraine with an initial €500 million ($558 million) contribution.

European Diplomats Refuse to Pose for Photo With Russia’s Lavrov at G20 — European diplomats refused to pose with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov on Friday, Oct. 30, forcing the US side to cancel the traditional G20 group photo. Lavrov attended the Atlanta meeting despite objections from several US and European lawmakers, while Ukraine was not invited at all. The meeting took place on the same day that Ukraine requested an emergency meeting of the UN Security Council, following Russia’s s

Ukraine Requests Emergency UN Security Council Meeting Over Russian Strikes — Ukraine requested an emergency meeting of the United Nations (UN) Security Council on Friday, Oct. 30, following Russia’s strikes that left at least 25 civilians killed and more than 110 wounded nationwide. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha reiterated that Moscow is using its permanent seat on the Security Council to block the body from fulfilling its mandate, while calling for tougher sanctions and more air defense.

Pope Leo XIV Votes in US Elections: First Time for a Pontiff — Robert Francis Prevost, known as Pope Leo XIV, has officially become the first pontiff ever to cast a vote in the US midterm elections on Friday, Oct. 30. He made the request as early as Oct. 3, as the mail ballot had to travel from Joliet, Illinois to Vatican City, Italy. While Prevost has voted regularly in Illinois for years, this is the first time he has done so after being elected pope in May 2025 – citing his belief that citize

Dnipro Station Hit Again as Russian Strikes Spark Fire — Russian forces again struck Dnipro’s railway station on the evening of Oct. 30, causing a fire and wounding a woman, the regional governor said. Ukrzaliznytsia confirmed multiple targeted strikes and said passengers and railway employees had taken shelter, with no casualties initially reported among those groups. The attack followed earlier strikes on the station, including one that killed 15 people on Oct. 29.

Ukraine Reports First Drone Interception of Russian KUB-2E Loitering Munition — Ukrainian pilots shot down a Russian KUB-2E loitering munition in the Zaporizhzhia sector using a General Chereshnia AIR interceptor, the National Association of Ukrainian Defense Industries said. The association described it as the first confirmed interception of the weapon by a frontline interceptor drone.

Lula’s Victory Preserves Kremlin Ties — Brazil’s election interrupted the advance of Trump-aligned governments in Latin America and preserved Lula’s commitment to BRICS. Alongside this week’s Russia-Africa summit, the result showcases Moscow’s continuing diplomatic and commercial relationships outside the West.

‘I Won’t Hold Back’: Estonian PM Refuses to Soften Criticism of Putin — Estonian Prime Minister Kristen Michal said he would not soften his criticism of Vladimir Putin following a Reuters report that Pentagon officials urged Baltic allies to moderate their rhetoric about Russia. Michal said he had received no such request personally and warned against appeasing dictators.

Su-57 Fighter Reportedly Burned Down at Russia’s Akhtubinsk Airfield — A Russian Su-57 fifth-generation stealth fighter reportedly burned down at the Astrakhan region’s Akhtubinsk airfield on Oct. 29 during an engine start-up incident. Russian officials have not confirmed the claim, and Kyiv Post is unable to independently verify the report. If the report is true, it would be the fourth Su-57 lost or damaged this year, after a Ukrainian drone strike in April and a crash near Moscow in July.

Ukraine Destroys Russian Iskander-M Launcher Near Key Transit Point — Ukraine’s Defense Forces struck an Iskander-M ballistic missile launcher near Fatezh in Russia’s Kursk region on Friday. They also hit six ammunition, logistics, and repair facilities in Russian-occupied Ukrainian territories, the General Staff said.

FSB Accuses 76-Year-Old Communist of Spying for Ukraine — Gennady Stepakhno, a former Communist Party leader and deputy speaker in Russia’s Murmansk region, has been detained on treason allegations. The FSB claims he passed government and infrastructure documents to Ukrainian military intelligence. A party colleague disputes the account, while local reporting suggests the case may concern a publicly announced pharmaceutical project.

Zelensky Ready to Discuss Territory With Putin, Sybiha Says — President Volodymyr Zelensky is ready to discuss territorial issues directly with Vladimir Putin, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said. Kyiv backed the Finnish and Norwegian leaders’ call with Putin to advance ceasefire efforts and secure a meeting. Sybiha also urged Europe to take a stronger diplomatic role while keeping the US involved.

Kyiv Builds Backup Crossings as Russia Targets Bridges — Construction of backup river crossings has begun in Kyiv as part of a nationwide plan for 21 alternative routes amid Russian attacks on bridges. The first crossings in the capital are expected to open in early 2027, Infrastructure Minister Mykola Kalashnyk said. Kyiv is also partially reopening its damaged South Bridge.

‘Inner Need to Engage With Heritage’ – Ukrainian Singer Khrystyna Soloviy on Stories Through Music — In an exclusive interview with Kyiv Post, Khrystyna Soloviy discusses reimagining Ukrainian music from the 1990s, artists’ responsibility toward their cultural heritage, and challenging Soviet-era stereotypes. She also reflects on performing for Ukrainian troops, women’s independence, damage to her studio from Russian attacks, and her upcoming musical projects.

‘Get Them There Alive’: Ukraine’s Railways Under Russian Barrage — Russia’s escalating attacks on Ukraine’s railway infrastructure have made train travel increasingly dangerous, forcing Ukrainian Railways to evacuate passengers whenever drone strikes threaten trains and stations. With hundreds of facilities damaged in 2026 and daily evacuations causing widespread delays, passengers and railway workers are adapting to wartime travel conditions as Ukraine braces for another difficult winter.

‘Dark Days for Ukraine and Europe’: Nahaylo Warns Ahead of US Midterms | Bohdan Nahaylo — Bohdan Nahaylo, editor-in-chief of the Kyiv Post, says the upcoming peace talks in Abu Dhabi have almost no chance of ending Russia’s war against Ukraine, giving their prospects just two out of ten.

Europe Launches $24 Billion Round of SAFE Funding, Focus on Ukraine — The European Commission announced the second funding round under the Security Action for Europe (SAFE) program on Thursday. All 27 EU Member States are eligible to apply for a share of the €21.3 billion ($24 billion) available in this tranche.

Independent Russian Newspaper Novaya Gazeta Shuts Under Kremlin Pressure — Russia’s independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced it was shutting down, blaming years of state pressure and repression over its critical reporting on the Kremlin and its war against Ukraine. The closure marks another blow to independent journalism in Russia, where the outlet faced license revocation, raids, arrests and accusations of being a “foreign agent.”

Pentagon Reportedly Urges Baltic States to Tone Down Russia Warnings — The Pentagon has privately urged Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia to moderate public warnings about Russia, Reuters reported. The messages come as Washington pushes for Ukraine peace talks and reviews US troop levels in Europe.

Ukrainian Soldier Suspected of Passing Troop Positions to Russia — Ukraine’s State Bureau of Investigation says a serviceman passed troop positions in Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions to Russia’s FSB, helping direct strikes that wounded Ukrainian soldiers. He is being held on suspicion of wartime treason and leaving his unit without authorization.

Oleshky Residents Leave for Ukraine, Russia as Truce Holds for 87 Hours — Ukraine and Russia have launched a coordinated humanitarian operation to deliver food, medical supplies, and other essentials to residents of Russian-occupied Oleshky in southern Ukraine, while offering civilians the opportunity to evacuate. The mission, prepared after weeks of negotiations and completed demining along designated routes, is being coordinated by the two countries’ human rights commissioners, Dmytro Lubinets

‘Entire Country, Not Just Oleshky’ – Zelensky Presses US Over Delay of Missiles — Russian strikes killed at least 20 people across Ukraine on Thursday, despite a US-brokered humanitarian ceasefire in occupied Oleshky. Zelensky urged Washington to push for nationwide de-escalation and approve urgently needed Patriot interceptors, warning that Moscow was preparing further ballistic attacks.

Putin Warns Europe War Will Not Produce Winners — Russian President Vladimir Putin said Russia is ready for a war with Europe but does not want one, warning that any escalation would have no winners. He also defended Finnish and Norwegian leaders for holding a phone call with him despite criticism from other European officials, while threatening to respond to challenges in the Baltic Sea.

UN Refugee Agency Says 9 Million Need Extra Winter Help — The UN refugee agency says nine million people in Ukraine, Syria, Lebanon and Afghanistan will need additional assistance to survive the coming winter. UNHCR is seeking at least $50 million for emergency winter support amid rising energy and food prices, fuel shortages and growing humanitarian needs. In Ukraine, temperatures could fall to -20C as Russian attacks continue to disrupt power supplies.

Ukrainian Drones Hit Russian Military Food Supplier, Oil Refinery in Overnight Attacks — Ukrainian drones struck the Novokuybyshevsk Oil Refinery in Russia’s Samara region, which produces jet fuel for the Russian military, marking the first reported refinery attack in nearly two weeks. Another strike hit a military food supplier in the Bryansk region, while drone attacks forced temporary closures at Moscow’s major airports.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, October 29, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on October 29, 2026.

Russian Attack Left Over 350,000 Without Power in Dnipro — Russian overnight attacks left more than 350,000 electricity customers without power in Dnipro and surrounding communities. Emergency crews worked to restore electricity as further strikes targeted industrial infrastructure in the Poltava region.

Russian Foreign Minister Arrives in US for G20 Amid Outcry — Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov arrived in Atlanta on Friday, Oct. 30 for the G20 foreign ministers’ meeting despite objections from US lawmakers and European allies. Moscow plans to challenge Western sanctions as Washington prepares new peace talks involving Ukraine and Russia.

Russia Strikes Kremenchuk Again: Kills 3, Injures 32 — Russian forces struck an industrial enterprise in Ukraine’s Kremenchuk district early on Friday, hours after a separate attack killed three civilians and injured 32, including six children. Poltava authorities declared a day of mourning.

Ukraine Pauses Strikes on Russian Refineries Under US Pressure – WSJ — Ukraine reportedly suspended strikes on Russian oil refineries following pressure from President Donald Trump ahead of the Nov. 3 US midterm elections. According to The Wall Street Journal, the unofficial pause could extend into November, even as Russia continues attacking Ukrainian cities and energy facilities.

UN Warns of Freezing Winter as Russian Strikes Threaten Ukraine’s Power — The UN refugee agency warns that nine million people in Ukraine, Syria, Lebanon, and Afghanistan need urgent winter assistance, as Russian attacks on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure threaten heating and electricity supplies.

Russian Ballistic Missile Strike on Kyiv Kills One, Sparks Fires — Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv late Thursday, killing at least one person, setting warehouses ablaze and damaging residential buildings and vehicles in two districts.

Oleshky Aid Convoy Ready to Depart as Demining Is Completed — Demining of routes into Russian-occupied Oleshky has been completed, Ukraine’s human rights commissioner Dmytro Lubinets said Thursday evening, Oct. 29, adding that a humanitarian convoy bound for the town’s central hospital is ready to depart. Residents will be able to leave until 2 p.m. local time, until aid distribution begins at 2:30 p.m. A Ukrainian and Russian delegation will observe the mission alongside a US journalistic crew

Putin Says Nordic Leaders Were Right to Call Him, Despite EU Criticism — Speaking at a press conference following the Russia-Africa summit on Thursday, Oct. 29, Russian President Vladimir Putin said Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre were right to call him despite criticism, arguing some Europeans want dialogue rather than Russia’s defeat. Although he voiced support for restoring ties with Europe, he warned that Moscow is ready for a war with the cont

Ukraine's Neptune Missiles Destroy 2 Russian Su-34 Bombers in Volgograd Region — Ukraine’s Neptune missiles destroyed two Russian Su-34 fighter-bombers at an airfield in Russia’s Volgograd region, the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine (AFU) reported on Thursday, Oct. 29. President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed the report, noting that an Iskander launcher was also hit. Meanwhile, intelligence points to new Russian ballistic missile attacks as Kyiv continues appealing to Western partners

Trilateral Delegation Arrives Ahead of Oleshky Aid Delivery as Newsmax Observers Draw Scrutiny — A delegation of Ukrainian, US and Russian representatives has reached the site from which aid will be delivered to Russian-occupied Oleshky on Friday, Oct. 30, Ukrainian lawmaker Davyd Arakhamia said Thursday. No US government authorities are reportedly expected on the ground, with a Newsmax crew representing the American side – which has drawn scrutiny from several media.

NBU Hikes Rate to 16.5% After Forecast Turns to Recession and Higher Inflation — The NBU lifted the key rate to 16.5% as it flipped its 2026 GDP forecast from 1.8% growth to a 0.4% contraction and raised its year-end inflation outlook to 12.5%. The central bank blamed Russian strikes on production and logistics, a port blockade and fuel prices. It plans to hold the rate until the Q2 of 2027.

Ukrainian Producer Oleg Kokhan: ‘The World Must See Ukraine Beyond War and Victimhood’ — Oleg Kokhan, founder of SOTA Cinema Group and invited to join the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences in 2026, discusses how Ukrainian cinema can break into global markets, challenge Russian cultural dominance, and turn international recognition into sustainable industry growth. In this interview with Kyiv Post, he talks about “War Through the Eyes of Animals,” international co-productions, and cinem

80% of Ukrainians Back Refinery Strikes Despite Risks of US Aid Cut — Four in five Ukrainians support continued strikes on Russian oil refineries even if Washington cuts or limits aid, a KIIS survey found. Respondents were asked to assume Moscow would make no reciprocal commitments to stop attacking Ukraine. The findings also show continued support for armed resistance despite the threat of winter blackouts.

EXPLAINED: Trump Jr.’s Russian Wedding Sponsor – What We Know About IB Challenger — Kyiv Post found that IB Challenger, the company that paid for Trump Jr.’s wedding festivities on behalf of a Russian oligarch, handles sponsorships for Russia’s International Boxing Association (IBA) and was tied to IBA events while Russian gas conglomerate Gazprom bankrolled the IBA in 2024. There are also few answers as to how Trump Jr. repaid the oligarch for the funds.

Russian Energy Firms Spend Over $87 Million on Anti-Drone Defenses — Russian energy companies and water utilities have spent more than $87 million on anti-drone defenses, according to Novaya Gazeta Europe. The investment comes as Ukrainian strikes have hit Russian energy infrastructure and sometimes disrupted electricity and heating supplies.

Putin Eyes Russian Factory Moves to Africa Amid Sanctions — Vladimir Putin said Russian companies are interested in moving some production to African countries amid sanctions against Russia’s economy. Speaking at the Russia-Africa summit in Moscow on Thursday, Oct. 29, he called for guarantees protecting Russian investments. His remarks came alongside proposals for industrial cooperation and a planned Russian bauxite venture in Ghana.

Russia May Use Oleshky Truce to Rebuild Forces – ISW — Russia could use the Oleshky humanitarian ceasefire to rebuild its forces, the ISW warned, while questioning safeguards for evacuees. The pause, which began on Oct. 27 and is scheduled to last until Nov. 1, is intended to allow aid deliveries and civilian departures. Ukrainian officials reported 54 hours without violations on Oct. 29.

Bodies Left Unburied, Stray Dogs Feeding on Corpses: Displaced Resident Reveals Life in Russian-Occupied Oleshky — In the interview, an anonymous resident of Oleshky, who has left the city, describes what Oleshky was like before the full-scale war. how life changed under occupation, and what is happening there now, according to her relatives.

Macron Says Russia Choosing ‘Escalation’ After Deadly Dnipro Train Station Strike in Ukraine — French President Emmanuel Macron accused Russia of choosing “escalation” over de-escalation after a Russian drone strike on Dnipro’s railway station killed 14 people. on Thursday The attack came amid continued Russian strikes across Ukraine and a fragile local ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky.

12th Kyiv International Economic Forum Held in Kyiv — Ukraine’s 12th Kyiv International Economic Forum focused on how businesses can withstand escalating Russian attacks, labour shortages and tighter EU trade restrictions. The government outlined plans to expand war-risk insurance, while business leaders stressed the need for predictable policies, workforce development and investment to sustain economic resilience.

UK Boosts Support to Ukraine with $13.3 Billion Package — The UK has announced its largest-ever single financial support package for Ukraine, pledging an additional £10 billion in military and economic assistance. The package includes urgent air defense funding to counter Russian attacks this winter, as well as guarantees to sustain essential services and strengthen Ukraine’s economy.

Russia Eases Fuel Rations in 15 Regions After Kyiv Halts Refinery Attacks — Russia has lifted fuel sales restrictions in 15 regions as supplies improve following a pause in Ukrainian strikes on oil refineries. However, fuel availability remains limited nationwide, and analysts warn that drivers should not expect significant price cuts despite recent declines in gasoline prices.

Day of Terror: Russian Strikes Kill 25, Wound At Least 110 Across Ukraine — Russian daytime strikes killed 20 people and injured at least 109 across Ukraine nationwide on Thursday, Oct. 29. Two 15-year-old girls were killed in central Chernihiv, while other attacks hit an apartment building in Kremenchuk and a railway platform in Dnipro. Later in the day, another drone hit the dormitory of a vocational school in Dnipro, setting several rooms on fire. Izium, Lozova and the Zaporizhzhia region wer

US Midterms: a Debacle for Trump? — The upcoming US midterm elections could reshape President Donald Trump’s ability to govern, with Democrats potentially gaining control of Congress. Commentators warn that an opposition majority may intensify Trump’s reliance on executive orders, deepen political divisions and test democratic institutions if he rejects defeat. For Europe and Ukraine, Democratic gains could provide greater congressional resistance to Trump’s policies, particularly regarding Russ

Germany’s KSK Special Forces Prepare for War Against Russia — After 30 years focused on hostage rescue, counter-terrorist operations, and high-risk reconnaissance, Germany’s elite KSK special forces unit is preparing for a potential military confrontation with Russia.

‘Kherson Feels Like It Did Before the War’ – Residents Describe Oleshky During Ceasefire — According to Kherson residents, a ceasefire is currently being observed in the city, prompting many people to take to the streets and travel into the city to collect belongings from their apartments – previously inaccessible due to drone attacks.

Ukrainian Delegation Heads Toward Oleshky for Aid Mission — A Ukrainian delegation led by Human Rights Commissioner Dmytro Lubinets set off toward Russian-occupied Oleshky on Thursday, Oct. 29, lawmaker David Arakhamia said. The mission aims to deliver humanitarian assistance and enable civilians to leave safely. Its preparations have included clearing mined routes under a localized ceasefire brokered with assistance from US First Lady Melania Trump.

Erdogan Offers Trump Help Reviving Ukraine-Russia Talks — Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan told Donald Trump that Ankara was ready to help revive diplomacy between Ukraine and Russia to end the war. The Wednesday call comes amid preparations for renewed trilateral negotiations. Turkey has previously offered to host talks, while Ukraine seeks concrete ceasefire steps and security guarantees.

Russia Cracks Down on Dating Chatbot ‘Exploited’ by Ukrainian Intelligence — The FSB and Internal Affairs Ministry say there has been an increase in the use by Ukrainian intelligence agencies of the “Davyinchik” chatbot on Telegram to recruit Russian youths to commit sabotage. It claims to have arrested almost 60 such individuals since July last year.

Russian Drone Strike on Dnipro Railway Platform Kills 14, Injures Over Dozen — A Russian jet-powered drone struck a railway platform in Dnipro where a passenger train bound for Zaporizhzhia was located, killing 14 people and injuring at least 14, Ukrainian authorities and the state railway operator said.

Poland to Transfer 2 MiG-29s to Ukraine in €50 Million Aid Package — Poland will transfer two MiG-29 fighter jets to Ukraine as part of a €50 million military aid package, a Polish defense official said. Warsaw is also considering a broader deal to exchange retired jets for Ukrainian drone technology, with President Karol Nawrocki signaling support in principle.

Two Belarussian Men Held in Germany Over Alleged Sabotage Plot — Two Belarussian men have been arrested in Germany on suspicion of plotting sabotage on behalf of a foreign power, reportedly Russia. A Ukrainian man has also been arrested in Poland over a suspected arson attack on a Romanian arms factory, as European authorities investigate alleged Russian-linked sabotage.

Kremlin Says Ukraine Peace Talks Hinge on Battlefield, Rejects European Role — Russia says renewed peace talks with Ukraine and the US could take place in Abu Dhabi after Nov. 4, but the Kremlin has yet to confirm a date and ruled out European participation as Kyiv points to Nov. 10 as a possible date.

Støre Rejects FT Report That Putin Spent 90-Minute Call Giving History Lecture — Norwegian PM Støre has rejected the Financial Times’ report that Putin spent most of a 90-minute call giving a lecture on medieval Slavic history. The newspaper stands by its reporting and has refused to issue a correction.

Poland is Trying to Insure Itself Against Another Yalta — Poland is deepening defense ties with the US and UK to make its security more important to allies. But as Washington, Moscow and Beijing may discuss Ukraine, Warsaw’s military investments cannot guarantee the US will prioritize Poland over a broader deal with Russia.

Ukraine Targets Russian Chemical Plants as Moscow Claims to Down Over 1200 Drones Overnight — Ukrainian drones reportedly targeted chemical facilities in Bashkortostan and the Tula Region on Oct. 28-29, including plants linked to Russia’s military industry. Moscow claimed its air defenses destroyed 1,214 Ukrainian drones overnight, as airport restrictions and damage reports spread across Russia.
ISW Russian Offensive Campaign Assessment, October 28, 2026 — War in Ukraine - Latest update, key takeaways and map from the Institute for the Study of War on October 28, 2026.

Russian Drones Strike Kharkiv Educational Facility, Attacks Across Ukraine Kill and Injure Civilians — Russian drones struck an educational institution in Kharkiv early Thursday, Oct. 29, while another attack sparked a fire elsewhere in the city. The overnight assault followed a series of Russian strikes on Wednesday that killed a man at a civilian enterprise in the Rivne region, wounded a worker in Dnipro, and injured civilians in the Chernihiv and Sumy regions. Ukrainian officials reported dam

Russia Uses North Korean Forced Labor to Sustain War Against Ukraine, Investigation Finds — A new investigation by The Hague-based Global Rights Compliance (GRC) has exposed a Russian recruitment network that places North Korean workers in factories supporting Moscow’s war against Ukraine, circumventing UN sanctions through student visas. Zelensky: No Energy Ceasefire With Russia, but Oleshky Truce Brings Hope — On Wednesday, President Volodymyr Zelensky said the proposed energy ceasefire between Ukraine and Russia never took effect because Moscow continued striking Ukrainian energy infrastructure.
